cases.title: gh-159428: Don't read mimetypes.knownfiles by default on Windows
cases.description:
Make knownfiles empty on Windows so that only the registry is used by default. Files passed to init() or assigned to knownfiles explicitly are still read.

The default knownfiles are POSIX paths such as /etc/mime.types. On Windows these resolve against the root of the current drive (e.g. C:\etc\mime.types), a location that unprivileged users can usually create.

cases.title: gh-158446: Reject float format precision near INT_MAX
cases.description:
PyOS_double_to_string() now raises ValueError("precision too big") for precisions above INT_MAX - 1024, matching what the format parsers already do above INT_MAX. Buffer size computations in pystrtod.c and dtoa.c add a few hundred to the precision using int / Py_ssize_t arithmetic and could wrap for such values, leading to a crash or incorrect output.

Also harden _Py_dg_dtoa() and rv_alloc() so their size arithmetic stays in range for any C caller.

---

This was reviewed and approved via the PSRT in a report which we'll make public soon as security releases are about to be cut tomorrow.

cases.title: gh-158973: Reset the warnings lock after fork in the child
cases.description:
Reset the warnings lock in the child after fork, before clearing other threads’ states. This prevents deadlocks when their finalizers issue warnings and the lock was held by a thread that no longer exists.  Record ownership before fork so the child can preserve the lock’s recursion depth and update its owner ID if  the forking thread held it.  Adds regression tests for child-cleanup warnings and recursive ownership across fork.

The PR was developed with assistance from GPT 6.1 Sol.

cases.title: gh-158816: Skip useless hash table probe when deleting from split dicts
cases.description:
# Summary

`delitem_common()` currently calls `lookdict_index()` before checking whether the dictionary is combined or split.

For split dictionaries, the returned hash-table slot is not used. Therefore, the probe performed by `lookdict_index()` is redundant for split-table deletions.

I propose moving `lookdict_index()` into the combined-table branch avoiding a full probe sequence for every deletion from a split dictionary.

# Benchmark
Measured with a free-threaded build, -Og, without PGO. The benchmark deletes keys from materialized instance dictionaries; medians over 12 alternating runs:

                        before   after    change
    del d[k]             71.2     69.2 ns/op   -2.8%
    d.pop(k)              98.9     96.1 ns/op   -2.8%
    colliding hashes      78.0     74.4 ns/op   -4.6%

Combined-table deletions are unchanged.

Clang also does not sink the `lookdict_index()` call into the branch at -O3 -DNDEBUG, so the improvement is not specific to the local -Og build.

# Validation

The following test modules pass:

- test_dict
- test_dictviews
- test_dictcomps

These could reasonably be classified as churn, however, the `turtle` module is, frankly, quite messy in places. I think these changes improve readability and, as a result, maintainability, so I intend to tidy up similar issues.

They should also have relatively little impact on useful Git history, since the majority of the affected lines date back to the original port in https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/97cf99fc7e8c56868711f7c91c3b1e37e4c66cba.

If there are no comments, I plan to merge this next Thursday.

cases.title: gh-98894: fix `CheckDtraceProbes` tests on Solaris
cases.description:
Solaris does not use the notes section to list available probes (`readelf -n <binary>` returns nothing), which makes the `test_check_probes` fail.

This PR adds a Solaris specific path which gets all the available probes by listing those available in the running test process instead.

The output below is very different so the comparison needs to be updated a little as well.

```
>>> import subprocess
>>> import os
>>> res = subprocess.run(["dtrace", "-l", "-P", f"python{os.getpid()}"])
   ID   PROVIDER            MODULE                          FUNCTION NAME
   34 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0                         sys_audit audit
   35 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0           sys_audit_tstate.part.0 audit
   36 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0             dtrace_function_entry function-entry
   37 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0          _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault function-entry
   38 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0            dtrace_function_return function-return
   39 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0          _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault function-return
   40 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0                   gc_collect_main gc-done
   41 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0                   gc_collect_main gc-start
   42 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0 import_find_and_load_with_name.isra.0 import-find-load-done
   43 python1427 libpython3.16.so.1.0 import_find_and_load_with_name.isra.0 import-find-load-start
```
A little unfortunate thing is that the test now requires elevated privileges, but that is true of all other DTrace tests as well, so I don't think that's a big deal.

BTW: there is Solaris specific ELF section for DTrace metadata and at first I wanted to fix the test by reading that one (with `readelf -p .SUNW_dof <binary>`). Unfortunately, the section includes more metadata than just available probes, and the now removed line probe is also present in the dumped strings (so `test_check_probes` passes, but `test_missing_probes` unexpectedly passes as well).

It's possible to use `elfdump` and do some binary parsing to extract only the available ones, but that is a huge overkill for a test like this. For those interested, the change is here: https://github.com/kulikjak/cpython/commit/564e946aa219d8d933a0ae7a7149a2d74c025a29
 

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-98894 -->
* Issue: gh-98894
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

cases.title: gh-159440: Pass --work-tree to the git commands used for the version tag
cases.description:
### Summary

The `GITTAG` build stamp uses `git --git-dir $(srcdir)/.git describe --all --always --dirty`. `--git-dir` does not imply a work tree, so git falls back to the current directory. In an out-of-tree build `make` runs in the build tree, where none of the tracked files exist, so the internal `diff-index HEAD` of `--dirty` reports every tracked file as deleted and the tag always comes out as `heads/<branch>-dirty` — even for a pristine checkout. In-tree builds never hit this, and `GITVERSION`/`GITBRANCH` don't touch the work tree, so only the dirty check was wrong.

Pass `--work-tree $(srcdir)` for all three commands. The semantics of `-dirty` are preserved (a genuinely modified source tree still reports `-dirty`), and in-tree builds are unchanged because `$(srcdir)` is `.`.

### Reproduce

sys.version reports a spurious -dirty git tag for out-of-tree builds, even when the checkout is pristine:
```console
$ mkdir -p ~/build/cpython && cd ~/build/cpython
$ bash ~/git/cpython/configure --prefix=$HOME/opt/cpython > /dev/null
$ make -j && make install -j
$ ~/opt/cpython/bin/python3 -VV
Python 3.16.0a1+dev (heads/main-dirty:25883627946, Oct 14 2026, 22:17:06) [GCC 11.4.0]
```

### Root cause
GITTAG uses git --git-dir $(srcdir)/.git describe --all --always --dirty. --git-dir does not imply a work tree, so git falls back to the current directory. In an out-of-tree build make runs in the build directory, where none of the tracked files exist, and the internal diff-index HEAD behind --dirty reports every tracked file as deleted. GITVERSION and GITBRANCH never touch the work tree, so only the dirty check was wrong.

### Change
All three git commands now get --work-tree $(srcdir):

```diff
-    GITTAG="git --git-dir \$(srcdir)/.git describe --all --always --dirty"
+    GITTAG="git --git-dir \$(srcdir)/.git --work-tree \$(srcdir) describe --all --always --dirty"
```
The semantics of -dirty are preserved: a genuinely modified source tree still reports -dirty, and in-tree builds are unchanged because $(srcdir) is ..


### Testing

- Out-of-tree build from a clean checkout: ./python -VV reports heads/main:<rev> instead of heads/main-dirty:<rev>.
- With an uncommitted change to a tracked file in the source tree, the rebuild correctly reports heads/main-dirty:<rev> again.
- In-tree build: the git commands resolve to the same values as before ($(srcdir) is .).
- git state checks / make regen-configure produce no further diff in configure, pyconfig.h.in or aclocal.m4.

### Issue
